text:
### Observed differences

- The successor profile of A20 changed completely. In the earlier window, all observed outgoing transitions of A20 went to A22 (200 of 200); in the later window, A20 leads into A30, A31 and A36 (about 33 in 100 transitions each) and back to A22 in only about 1 in 200 cases. This difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits [DIR014].
- A21 changed in the complementary direction. Earlier, its outgoing transitions split across A36 (about 38 in 100), A30 (about 34) and A31 (about 28); in the later window, about 995 in 1000 go directly to A25 [DIR015].
- The block A30/A31/A36 changed its exit. Earlier, each block member passed on to A25 in roughly 28–37 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window, each passes to A22 in about 31–34 in 100, and transitions to A25 have nearly disappeared (about 1 in 200). The block's internal behaviour is essentially unchanged: its members still co-occur in every trace and appear in both orders in similar proportions in both windows [DIR018, DIR019, DIR024, REL007, REL008, REL009].
- Order relations between the block and A21/A22 reversed. Earlier, A21 preceded each block member, and A22 preceded each block member, in 100 in 100 traces; in the later window, each block member precedes A21 and precedes A22 in about 995 in 1000 traces, while the activities still co-occur in every trace [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006].
- Step distances swapped. A22 followed A20 within one event in all earlier traces but about four events later in about 995 in 1000 later traces; A25 followed A21 four events earlier in all traces but within one event in about 995 in 1000 later traces. The ordered pairs A21→block member and block member→A25 within five events, present in 200 earlier traces, appear in only 1 later trace [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG009, LAG012].
- Event positions shifted accordingly: the block members now occur earlier (mean position about 0.59 → 0.41 of the trace), A22 later (about 0.38 → 0.47) and A21 later (about 0.53 → 0.62), while A20 and A25 keep their positions; all seven activities still occur in every trace in both windows [POS005, POS006, POS007, POS003, POS002, POS001, POS004].
- Away from this segment, smaller shifts appear: about 6 in 100 cases moved from the A02-led block (A02/A06/A07/A08 present in 111 → 99 of 200 traces) to the A01-led block (A01/A03/A04/A05, 89 → 101), and after A02 the share continuing to A07 rose from about 28 to 44 in 100; after A25, the choice between A16 and A17 shifted (107/93 → 119/81 of 200 traces) and between A18 and A19 (92/108 → 109/91); A10 and A11 repeat slightly more often (about 1.58 → 1.72 occurrences per trace) and A13 participation fell (55 → 42 of 200 traces) [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, DIR002, OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, OCC018, OCC009, OCC010, OCC012].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the flow around A20, A21, A22, A25 and the block A30/A31/A36 was re-wired. In the earlier window, A20 passed directly to A22 while A21 fed the three-activity block, which converged on A25; in the later window, A20 feeds that same block, the block converges on A22, and A21 passes directly to A25 — in effect, the block moved from A21's branch to A20's branch and its exit changed from A25 to A22 [DIR014, DIR015, DIR018, DIR019, DIR024, REL001, REL004, LAG001, LAG002].

The change is shown directly and consistently: five successor profiles changed almost completely (each difference larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits), six order relations flipped from 100 in 100 one way to about 995 in 1000 the other way, the A20→A22 and A21→A25 step distances swapped between one and four events, and the positional shifts match the new wiring. Because every involved activity occurs in all traces in both windows and the block's internal mixed order is preserved, this is a change in ordering constraints, not activities appearing, disappearing or repeating differently [POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS001, POS004, REL007, REL008, REL009]. The items are, however, highly dependent — they all describe one underlying re-wiring rather than independent confirmations — and the observations cannot distinguish which equivalent re-wiring occurred (relocating the block onto A20's path versus re-targeting the block's exit from A25 to A22 while connecting A21 directly to A25), since both produce the same relational pattern [DIR014, DIR015, REL001, LAG001].

Other differences: the modest shifts in the A01/A02 blocks, the A16–A19 choices after A25, the slightly higher repetition of A10/A11 and the lower participation of A13 are not explained by this hypothesis; at a few percentage points on 200-trace windows, they could also reflect sampling variation between the two windows [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002, OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, OCC018, OCC009, OCC012].
